counterfactual_missing_items: No fibrinoid necrosis or thrombosis is present, limiting the called definitive vasculitic change.
Confluent epidermal detachment, mucosal involvement, or a drug-exposure timeline are not supplied to support TEN.
Direct viral detection for VZV/HSV/SARS-CoV-2 in the skin is negative, arguing against varicella.
decisive_items: Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis
Early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels without fibrinoid necrosis or thrombosis
Diagnostic testing on superficial skin sample for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 viruses (all negative)
response.rationale: R1 is the strongest because the purpuric rash aligns with the raw vascular and dermal findings of an early-stage vasculitic process, while R3 is excluded by negative direct skin viral testing. R2 is the closest runner-up because it captures only the epidermal necrolysis component, but its histologic overlap with viral cytopathy, non-confluent purpuric phenotype, and absence of mucosal/full-thickness blistering render TEN less fitting.

rejected.why: The papulovesicular morphology and multinucleated keratinocytes could suggest varicella, but diagnostic skin testing was explicitly negative for VZV, HSV, and SARS-CoV-2 by viral tests and IHC, so varicella is not the most likely diagnosis.
